analysis.title: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.: Capital budget toward advanced nodes; investing into frontier labs and semis chain
key_insights: BofA maintains Buy on TSMC with a PO of NT$3,260 (US$620 per ADR), based on 20x 2027E P/E. The stock was NT$2,285 (US$388.62 ADR) at publication.
TSMC's board approved capital appropriations of US$41bn, putting the budget +116% YoY in 2026.
56% of the 2026 budget relates to advanced front-end process expansion and upgrade, the highest share since 2022. BofA reads this as a steep capacity ramp on 3nm and 2nm.

Accumulated capital appropriation is +50% YoY, above the long-term trend of +40-45%. This could lift 2027 capex to US$80-90bn, versus BofA's US$83bn and Street ~US$80bn. BofA's 2026 capex estimate is US$62bn.
BofA's model shows advanced node utilization still above 100% in 2027. It could stay healthy in 2028 even if AI demand moderates or declines.
The board raised the quarterly dividend from NT$7 to NT$9 per share, effective for 3Q26 earnings, for a payout ratio of ~30%. The annual cash outflow is ~US$29bn.
BofA estimates FCF rising from US$53bn in 2026 to US$76bn in 2027 and US$109bn in 2028, which covers the dividend.

The board approved investing up to US$1bn in frontier AI labs and is setting up a wholly owned VC arm for strategic investments in the semiconductor chain. The report cites TSMC's prior IPO investment in ARM in 2023 (US$100mn) as a strategic move with suppliers and partners.

Valuation is 15x/13x 2027/28E P/E against a historical 11-21x range, on a 34% EPS CAGR. BofA calls this undemanding and potentially defensive given TSMC's technology leadership and a benign competitive landscape.
BofA's EPS estimates are above Visible Alpha consensus: NT$111.88 vs 111.29 for 2026, NT$159.09 vs 150.60 for 2027, NT$200.99 vs 191.73 for 2028.

market_movers.rationale: BofA keeps Buy on a 20x 2027E P/E. It cites the steep advanced-node capacity ramp, a higher dividend and an undemanding multiple against 34% EPS CAGR.

sector_views.rationale: BofA is structurally positive on TSMC as the leading contract chipmaker, expecting over 15% growth with rising FCF from 2026. Advanced node utilization stays above 100% in 2027.

earnings_insights: BofA 2026E EPS NT$111.88 (+68.9% YoY) vs Visible Alpha consensus NT$111.29. These are estimates, not reported results.
BofA 2027E EPS NT$159.09 (+42.2% YoY) vs Visible Alpha consensus NT$150.60. These are estimates.
BofA 2028E EPS NT$200.99 (+26.3% YoY) vs Visible Alpha consensus NT$191.73. These are estimates.
2025A EPS was NT$66.24 (+46.4% YoY) and 2024A EPS was NT$45.24, per BofA's table. Net income (adjusted) was NT$1,717,886mn in 2025A.
BofA ADR EPS estimates: US$16.98 for 2026E, US$24.14 for 2027E, US$30.50 for 2028E.
BofA estimates sales of NT$5,594,068mn for 2026E, NT$7,852,781mn for 2027E and NT$9,653,190mn for 2028E. Operating margin estimates are 58.8%, 60.8% and 62.2%.

trade_ideas.description: Long TSM (ADR) / TSMC 2330 TT, Buy rating with PO US$620 per ADR (NT$3,260)
trade_ideas.rationale: The stock is undemanding at 15x 2027E P/E on a 34% EPS CAGR, with a benign competitive landscape and advanced node utilization above 100% in 2027.
trade_ideas.risk: Smartphone/consumer electronics slowdown, Intel foundry insourcing ambitions, advanced node execution risk, higher tariffs.

risk_factors: A greater-than-expected slowdown in global smartphone and consumer electronics demand.
Intel's potential insourcing strategy and ambitions in foundry services.
AI demand moderating or declining. BofA says utilization could stay healthy in 2028 even in that case.
